message.content:
Below are two ways you can create a **Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.  
(If you’re actually on AWS you would use `aws ec2 run-instances` instead – but the wording “Google Cloud” + “EC2” suggests you mean GCP’s Compute Engine.)

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Pick a name, zone, and machine‑type that fits your workload
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # e.g. us-central1-a, europe-west4-b, etc.
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed

# 2. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --labels=purpose=demo,gpu=RTX-A6000
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Where the VM lives (must match your GPU availability). |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM profile. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `count=1` gives you one RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 100 GB (adjust if you need more). |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keeps the VM running during maintenance events. |
| `--scopes` | Gives the VM full Cloud Platform access (you can tighten this later). |
| `--labels` | Optional metadata tags for cost allocation, automation, etc. |

> **Tip:** If you need more than one GPU, just change `count=2`, `count=4`, etc. (subject to quota).

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON body)

If you prefer to hit the Compute Engine REST endpoint directly (e.g., from a custom script or Terraform provider), here’s the minimal payload you’d POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "labels": {
    "purpose": "demo",
    "gpu": "RTX-A6000"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`, and `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` with your actual values.  
The `startup-script` installs the NVIDIA driver automatically after the VM boots.

---

## Quick Checklist Before Running

1. **Enable APIs** – Make sure the *Compute Engine API* is enabled for your project (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).
2. **GPU Quota** – Verify you have enough GPU quota in the chosen zone (`gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="zone:{ZONE}"`).
3. **Billing** – Ensure billing is attached to the project; GPU instances incur extra charges.
4. **Firewall Rules** – By default the `default` network allows SSH; if you need other ports open, add firewall rules.
5. **IAM Permissions** – You need `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` (or equivalent) to create instances.

Once you run either the `gcloud` command or the REST POST, you’ll see the instance appear in the console under *Compute Engine → VM instances*. After a minute or so, the VM will be ready, and you can SSH into it (`gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --zone=$ZONE`) to start working.
